name: Sri Lanka
officialName: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

healthInfo.emergencyNumber: 110 (police), 1990 (government emergency hotline — ambulance/fire/police), 011-269-1111 (national hospital emergency line in Colombo)
healthInfo.healthcareSystem: Universal (free public healthcare for residents). Tourists can access both public and private facilities. Private hospitals in Colombo are significantly better than public ones. No health coverage for tourists — pay out-of-pocket.
healthInfo.qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is mixed. Colombo has several excellent private hospitals with internationally trained doctors and English-speaking staff (Nawaloka Hospital, Lanka Hospital, Asiri Surgical). Public hospitals in Colombo are adequate for basic emergencies but can be overcrowded. Rural areas have very limited facilities. Private hospitals in Colombo are the best option for tourists.
healthInfo.pharmacyHours: Pharmacies are widely available in cities and towns, typically open 8am-9pm. Some 24-hour pharmacies in Colombo. Pharmacies are commonly called 'Medical Halls' or 'Dispensaries' in Sri Lanka.
healthInfo.pharmacyTips: Many common OTC medications are available. Some antibiotics and other prescription drugs are available OTC in Sri Lanka — this is common practice. Generic medications are widely available. Bring your prescription as backup. Quality of medications is generally good at reputable pharmacies.
healthInfo.prescriptionRules: Prescription requirements are not always strictly enforced. However, for controlled substances, carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter. Sri Lankan doctors at private hospitals can easily re-prescribe if needed.

restrictedMeds.name: Diazepam (Valium) and benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires prescription. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter. Quantities for personal use are permitted with documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires prescription. Bring your documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription. Bring your documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Requires Sri Lankan prescription or special permission. Contact the Sri Lankan embassy before traveling with ADHD medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Sri Lanka. It was historically used medicinally but is now prohibited. Do not bring any cannabis products.

healthInfo.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring sufficient supplies — some specialty medications may not be available. For controlled substances, carry the original prescription.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not required but strongly recommended for all travelers.
travelInsurance.tips: Healthcare at private hospitals in Colombo is affordable by Western standards — a specialist consultation costs 2,000-5,000 LKR ($6-15 USD). However, serious medical conditions may require evacuation to Singapore or India. Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is strongly recommended.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, and Typhoid are recommended due to variable food/water safety. Consider Japanese Encephalitis vaccination for extended rural stays.

healthInfo.waterNotes: Tap water is not reliably safe outside major cities. Drink bottled or purified water in most areas. In Colombo, tap water is technically treated but many people still prefer bottled. Bottled water is widely available and inexpensive.
healthInfo.foodSafetyTips: Be cautious with food. Sri Lankan cuisine (rice and curry, hoppers, kottu) is generally safe at restaurants. Avoid raw salads unless you trust the establishment. Peel fruits or wash with purified water. Street food can cause issues — start with lighter options. Spicy food is the norm — start slowly.
healthInfo.medicalTourismNote: Sri Lanka is not a major medical tourism destination but does attract some medical tourists for affordable surgeries, especially from the Maldives and other nearby countries. Quality at top private hospitals in Colombo is good.
